questions.question: What tag does predict_mft use for a token it never saw during training?
options: The globally most frequent tag returned as default_tag
The tag of the previous token in the sentence
A random tag from the training vocabulary
An empty string that marks a parse boundary
questions.explanation: train_mft counts all tags and returns all_tags.most_common(1)[0][0] as the unknown-word fallback.

questions.question: What does train_hmm store in emissions[tag]?
options: Counts of transitions from that tag to the next tag
Counts of lowercased tokens emitted by that tag
The final Viterbi path for each sentence
Only the sentence lengths for that tag
questions.explanation: For each token/tag pair, train_hmm increments emissions[tag][token.lower()].

questions.question: Why does viterbi pass alpha to log_prob for an unseen token?
options: Alpha changes the token into a verb
Alpha removes all transition probabilities from the path
Smoothing keeps the emission probability finite instead of taking log(0)
Smoothing guarantees the unseen token is the best tag
questions.explanation: The numerator adds alpha and the denominator includes the vocabulary size, giving unknown emissions a small nonzero probability.

questions.question: What does the Viterbi dynamic program optimize?
options: The shortest sequence of words regardless of grammar
The most common tag independently at every position
The number of unique tokens in the sentence
The highest-scoring sequence of tags using emissions and tag transitions
questions.explanation: Each state stores the best score ending in a tag and a backpointer to reconstruct the globally best path.

questions.question: Which transition is used to initialize the first Viterbi column?
options: The transition from <BOS> to each candidate tag
The transition from <EOS> to each candidate tag
A transition from the first word to itself
No transition; only the emission is scored
questions.explanation: train_hmm records a <BOS> transition for the first tag, and viterbi combines that log probability with the first emission.

questions.question: Why can a sequence model outperform most-frequent-tag tagging on an ambiguous word?
options: It ignores the word identity and uses only sentence length
It scores the word's emission together with neighboring tag transitions
It assigns every unknown token the same noun tag
It replaces POS tags with character n-grams
questions.explanation: The HMM can prefer a tag whose surrounding transitions make sense even when the token's local evidence is ambiguous.
